audit.why: 51.35% over 1924 games — the largest sample in my slice — matching MC_WR_TABLES. No elo-tier language present.

audit.whatIsWrong: SMOKE SCREEN DOES NOT BLIND, and the entry gives explicit tactical advice built on the belief that it does. content mid: 'Note his Smoke Screen blinds your empowered Siphoning Strike (it's an auto, so the blind makes it whiff) — don't throw a stacked Q into the smoke.' The same 'W blind' wording appears in whys[2] and early.
audit.why: Riot's text for Smoke Screen: 'Graves fires a smoke canister at the target area creating a cloud of smoke that REDUCES SIGHT RANGE. Enemies caught in the initial impact are dealt magic damage and have their Move Speed reduced briefly.' Its kit flags are projectile, slow and zone — there is no blind, and nothing in the ability causes attacks to miss. It is a nearsight, which limits how far Nasus can SEE, not whether his attacks land. At Siphoning Strike's 255 range Nasus is standing on top of Graves and can see him fine. So the advice is not merely wrong, it is expensively wrong: it tells a Nasus to withhold the one ability he has spent the entire game stacking, at the exact moment he is in range to use it. The correct read is the inverse — Smoke Screen is how Graves BREAKS AWAY, because you lose sight of him if he leaves your immediate radius, so the answer is to stay on top of him and keep swinging.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen is a nearsight and a slow, not a blind. Your stacked Q lands in it normally — the danger is losing sight of him, so stay glued to him.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (W Smoke Screen description, flags projectile/slow/zone)

audit.whatIsWrong: New Destiny is described as 'shotgun autos', '4-shell spread' and 'shell magazine' throughout, but neither layer mentions the single most exploitable property of it.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Attacks fire 4 bullets, which CANNOT PASS THROUGH UNITS.' Graves's basic attacks are stopped outright by any unit in the way, minions included. For a melee stacker whose entire lane plan is farming behind his own wave, that means the wave is not just cover from poke — it is a hard wall against his primary damage. Nothing in either layer connects the two, even though the entry already tells the player to farm from behind minions for other reasons.
audit.corrected: His bullets cannot pass through units. Keep a minion between you and his autos simply do not reach.

audit.whatIsWrong: The entry is built entirely around Wither timing versus Quickdraw — 'never get caught with it on cooldown' — yet gives neither cooldown, and misses that Quickdraw's cooldown is not fixed.
audit.why: Quickdraw is 16/15/14/13/12s and Wither is 15/14/13/12/11s, so Wither is exactly one second shorter at every rank. On paper Nasus out-cycles the dash. But Riot's text adds: 'Hitting enemies with basic attacks LOWERS THE COOLDOWN of this skill.' So that one-second edge only survives while Graves is not freely auto-attacking. Chain that with New Destiny's bullets being blocked by units and you get the actual lane plan, which neither layer states: stand behind the wave, his autos are stopped, his Quickdraw cooldown stops being reduced, and Wither goes back to out-cycling his dash. Three kit facts that only mean something together.
audit.corrected: Wither is 15s against Quickdraw's 16s — you out-cycle him by a second, but only while his autos are blocked, because hitting you refunds his dash cooldown.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (E Quickdraw cooldown 16/15/14/13/12 and description, P New Destiny)

audit.whatIsWrong: End of the Line is named correctly and described as a cone, but its terrain behaviour is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Graves fires an explosive shell that detonates after 1 second, OR AFTER COLLIDING WITH TERRAIN', and the kit carries the terrain flag. Fighting with a wall at your back changes when and where the detonation happens rather than letting the shell run its full timer. For a champion who cannot dash out of the cone, where he chooses to stand relative to terrain is one of the few free variables he controls.
audit.corrected: End of the Line detonates early on terrain — a wall at your back changes where the cone lands.
sources: champ-data/_kits/graves.json (Q End of the Line description, terrain flag)

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4].why is the cross-matchup boilerplate 'Fury of the Sands flips dives ... First real fight you're allowed to take', while its own side says Graves and content whys[4] calls level 6 'his best all-in window'.
audit.why: The layers disagree about the same stage. Collateral Damage plus a full magazine plus a Q cone is a real burst window against a Nasus who has not yet stacked, and the content layer says so. The boilerplate would send the player into it.
audit.corrected: Rewrite as his burst window, and give the actual counter — deny the autos.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[6].side is 'Skill' while its own why reads '300+ stacks and two items: you out-duel Graves on cooldown and three-shot his tower', and content win[6] is 'Nasus'. This matchup has the largest layer divergence in the slice alongside Fiora — full sides [Graves x5, Skill, Skill] against content [Skill, Nasus, Graves, Nasus, Graves, Graves, Nasus], disagreeing at five of seven stages.
audit.why: Only stage 6 is internally contradictory, so only stage 6 is edited. The content layer's chart here is notably more granular than the full layer's flat run of enemy-favoured stages, and it tracks the real shape of the lane — Nasus genuinely takes level 2 once Wither is online against a champion whose whole kit is kiting. The full layer looks templated.
audit.corrected: phases[6].side = Nasus. The other four disagreements flagged, not edited.

audit.why: The packet's suspectNames hit on 'His Collateral Damage' in whys[4] is a FALSE POSITIVE — that is Graves's real R name. Ability naming in this entry is otherwise the best in my slice: Quickdraw, End of the Line, Collateral Damage, Smoke Screen and True Grit are all named and all correct. The Smoke Screen error is about what the ability DOES, not what it is called, which is why no name-matching detector caught it.

notes:
HIGHEST-VALUE FIX IN THIS MATCHUP: content mid tells the player 'his Smoke Screen blinds your empowered Siphoning Strike (it's an auto, so the blind makes it whiff) — don't throw a stacked Q into the smoke.' Smoke Screen does not blind. It reduces SIGHT RANGE and slows on impact; its kit flags are projectile, slow, zone, with no blind anywhere. Graves's W has not been a blind since the champion was reworked. The cost of this error is unusually high because it instructs a Nasus to withhold the one ability he has spent the whole game stacking, at the exact moment he is close enough to land it. The correct reading is the opposite: the nearsight is how Graves DISENGAGES, so the answer is to stay glued to him. Three strings carried the 'W blind' wording; I corrected all three.

Second finding, and the one I would most like carried into other Graves matchups: New Destiny's four bullets CANNOT PASS THROUGH UNITS. A single minion between Nasus and Graves eats the entire auto-attack volley. Neither layer mentions it anywhere, despite the entry already telling the player to farm behind the wave for unrelated reasons.

Those two combine into a lane plan that no single field currently states. Wither (15s) is one second shorter than Quickdraw (16s) at every rank, so Nasus out-cycles the dash — BUT Quickdraw's cooldown is reduced when Graves lands basic attacks, so the edge only exists while his autos are being blocked. Wave positioning is therefore not just damage mitigation, it is what keeps Nasus's only cooldown ahead of his. Three separate kit facts that are individually unremarkable and jointly decisive.

This is otherwise the strongest content entry in my slice — 3 sequencing cues, and Quickdraw, End of the Line, Collateral Damage, Smoke Screen and True Grit all named correctly. Which is exactly why the Smoke Screen error is worth flagging loudly: the entry reads authoritative, and the one thing it gets wrong it states with more specificity and confidence than anything else in the file ('it's an auto, so the blind makes it whiff'). The packet's detector cannot catch this class of error at all — the ability NAME is right, only its described behaviour is wrong. Across my nine matchups the detector produced six flags, all six false positives, while missing one fabricated name (Gnar 'Quickness'), one fabricated mechanic (Gragas 'Q pool'), one fabricated heal (Darius 'passive heal'), one wrong ability property (this one) and one wrong ability class (Galio 'global R').
